learn.title: Compute design: VM-based solutions and batch processing
objectives: Specify VM components from workload requirements: VM family and size, managed disk type, ephemeral OS disks and local storage
Choose a pricing model for compute: pay-as-you-go, Spot, reservations, savings plan for compute and Azure Hybrid Benefit
Recommend VM-based solutions: Virtual Machine Scale Sets, Azure Dedicated Host, Azure Virtual Desktop, Azure VMware Solution, confidential VMs and trusted launch
Manage VM images and software at scale with Azure Compute Gallery, VM Image Builder and VM Applications
Design batch and HPC processing with Azure Batch (pools, jobs, tasks, Spot nodes, auto pools, MPI) and choose between Batch, AKS jobs, Functions and Container Apps jobs
concepts: VM size naming

Family letter plus suffixes: a = AMD, p = Arm (Cobalt), d = local temp disk, s = premium storage capable. D = general purpose, E = memory optimized, F = compute optimized, L = storage optimized, M = very large memory, N = GPU, H = HPC, B = burstable.
Managed disk types

Ultra Disk (highest IOPS, data disks only), Premium SSD v2 (adjustable IOPS/throughput, data disks only, no host caching), Premium SSD (fixed tiers, bursting, OS or data), Standard SSD (web/dev-test), Standard HDD (backup, noncritical; OS disk use retiring September 8, 2028).
Premium SSD v2

Every disk gets 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s free; you pay for capacity plus any extra IOPS and throughput, and you can change performance up to four times in 24 hours without downtime. Most often the best price-performance for databases.
Ephemeral OS disk

OS disk created on the VM's local cache, temp or NVMe storage. Lower latency and fast reimage for stateless workloads. No stop-deallocate, snapshots, image capture, Azure Backup or Site Recovery; data is lost on resize, redeploy or service healing.
Azure Spot VMs

Spare capacity at a deep discount, no SLA, evicted with up to 30 seconds notice through Scheduled Events. Eviction policy Deallocate (default, disks still billed) or Delete. Max price -1 means no price-based eviction. B-series is not supported.
Reservations vs savings plan

Reservations commit to a specific product, family and region for 1 or 3 years and give the deepest discount for stable usage. A compute savings plan commits to an hourly spend for 1 or 3 years across regions and eligible services. Reservations are applied first.
Azure Dedicated Host

A whole physical server for one subscription. Gives hardware isolation, maintenance control (defer platform updates within a 35-day rolling window) and Azure Hybrid Benefit. Billed per host; VMs on it show a price of 0. A host runs VM sizes from one series only.
Confidential VMs vs trusted launch

Trusted launch (default for new Gen2 VMs, no extra cost) adds Secure Boot, vTPM and boot integrity monitoring. Confidential VMs (DCasv5/ECasv5 AMD SEV-SNP, DCesv6/ECesv6 Intel TDX) also encrypt memory in use and isolate the VM from the host, with attestation, and no code changes.
Azure Compute Gallery and VM Applications

The gallery stores versioned image definitions and replicates them to target regions. VM Applications are versioned software packages in the same gallery, installed on VMs and scale sets with ordering and Azure Policy enforcement, so you don't need to rebuild the image.
Azure Virtual Desktop

Pooled host pools (multi-session Windows 11 Enterprise, breadth-first or depth-first load balancing, FSLogix profiles) or personal host pools (one VM per user). Scaling plans and Start VM on Connect cut cost; RemoteApp groups publish single apps.
Azure VMware Solution

VMware vSphere private clouds on dedicated bare-metal Azure hosts (minimum three hosts per cluster). Microsoft manages ESXi, vCenter, vSAN and NSX lifecycle. HCX migrates VMs without re-IP; ExpressRoute Global Reach connects on-premises.
Azure Batch

Managed job scheduling and VM pools. Pool = compute nodes; job = collection of tasks on a pool; task = command line on a node. Start tasks, application packages, autoscale formulas, auto pools, job schedules, task dependencies and multi-instance (MPI) tasks. No extra charge beyond the compute and storage used.
comparisons: Ultra Disk vs Premium SSD v2 vs Premium SSD

Ultra for extreme IOPS (up to 400,000) and the lowest latency; Premium SSD v2 for most production databases at a lower price; Premium SSD when you need an OS disk, host caching, bursting or availability sets.
Spot vs reservation vs savings plan

Spot for interruptible work at the lowest price; a reservation for steady 24x7 VMs of a known family and region; a savings plan when VM series, regions or services change. Azure Hybrid Benefit covers licences on top of any of them.

Dedicated Host isolates the physical server from other customers and gives maintenance control. A confidential VM protects data in use from the host and operator through hardware memory encryption. These meet different requirements.
AVD pooled vs personal vs Windows 365

Pooled: many users per multi-session host, lowest cost for task workers. Personal: a persistent dedicated VM for each user who needs admin rights. Windows 365: a fixed per-user Cloud PC price with little infrastructure to manage.
Batch vs AKS jobs vs Container Apps jobs vs Functions

Batch for large-scale parallel, HPC, MPI or GPU work with VM-level control. AKS jobs when a cluster and Kubernetes skills already exist. Container Apps jobs for serverless containerized scheduled or event-driven runs. Functions for short event-driven work and fan-out.
Azure VMware Solution vs Azure VMs
AVS for a fast VMware datacenter exit that keeps vSphere tools and IP addresses. It's billed per dedicated host. Azure VMs for workloads you can rehost per VM and right-size individually.
traps: Ultra Disk and Premium SSD v2 cannot be OS disks and don't support host caching; pair them with a Premium SSD OS disk.
Ephemeral OS disk VMs cannot be stop-deallocated, backed up with Azure Backup or replicated with Site Recovery, and Batch doesn't support ephemeral OS disks on Spot nodes.
Spot VMs cannot be converted to or from standard VMs after creation, and long tightly coupled MPI jobs are a poor fit for Spot because one eviction can restart the whole job.
Multi-instance (MPI) tasks in Batch need inter-node communication enabled and taskSlotsPerNode set to 1, or they stay in the active state forever.
Trusted launch doesn't support managed images; use Azure Compute Gallery image versions instead.
A compute savings plan doesn't cover storage, networking or software licences, and it cannot be cancelled. Use Azure Hybrid Benefit for licences.
revision: Match the family to the bottleneck: E for memory, F for CPU, L for local NVMe, M for SAP HANA, HB for memory bandwidth (CFD), ND for AI training, NV for graphics.
Premium SSD v2 is usually the best value for databases; choose Ultra only when you need more IOPS than Premium SSD v2 provides or the lowest latency.
Reserve the steady baseline, use Spot or Spot Priority Mix (Flexible scale sets) for interruptible burst, and add Azure Hybrid Benefit for Windows Server and SQL Server licences.
Dedicated Host is for physical isolation and maintenance control; confidential VMs are for protecting data in use; trusted launch is the baseline for every Gen2 VM.
In AVD, depth-first load balancing with a session limit and a scaling plan lowers cost, and breadth-first gives the best user experience.
AVS is the answer for a quick VMware exit without re-IP; use HCX for migration and ExpressRoute Global Reach for connectivity.
In Batch, use a start task to install software on each node, application packages for versioned binaries, an auto pool for a pool per job, and Spot nodes with a dedicated baseline for cheap progress.
Choose Batch for HPC, MPI and very large parallel work; Container Apps jobs for serverless container runs; AKS jobs only when a cluster already exists.

questions.on: Recommend a compute solution for batch processing

questions.e: Spot nodes in Batch can be preempted at any time. A dedicated baseline keeps the job moving.

Pauses the task and resumes it on the same node later

questions.on: Recommend a compute solution for batch processing
questions.q: A tightly coupled CFD solver uses MPI across 64 nodes and needs low-latency interconnect. Runs take 12 hours and mustn't be restarted halfway through. Which Azure Batch design should you recommend?
opts: Spot-only HB-series nodes with multi-instance tasks and checkpointing off
Dedicated RDMA-capable HB-series nodes with inter-node communication and multi-instance tasks
Container Apps jobs with parallelism set to 64 replicas
F-series dedicated nodes with four task slots per node and no MPI
questions.e: A long MPI job is a poor fit for Spot, because one preemption reruns the whole job. Multi-instance tasks need inter-node communication.

questions.on: Recommend a compute solution for batch processing

A Batch account in Batch service mode with pools in a virtual network

questions.e: In user subscription mode, pool VMs are created in your subscription. This mode needs a Key Vault in the same subscription and region.

questions.on: Recommend a compute solution for batch processing
questions.q: A Batch design uses Spot nodes with ephemeral OS disks to speed up node start-up. Pool creation for the Spot nodes fails. What is the cause?

questions.e: Batch uses a service-managed Stop-Deallocate eviction policy for Spot nodes, and ephemeral OS disks don't support it.
